content.title: About
content.content: Cocktail sauce is a thick, flavorful condiment typically made from tomato ketchup, horseradish, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and spices. It is traditionally served with seafood, especially shrimp cocktail, but also works as a dip for fish, chicken, and vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cocktail sauce recipes appeared in the United States in the early 20th century.
The classic American version contains horseradish, while European variants often replace it with Worcestershire or soy sauce.
Cocktail sauce is commonly served in small glasses alongside shrimp cocktail in seafood restaurants.
Many variations exist: spicier versions add Tabasco, sweeter ones incorporate honey or brown sugar.
In Japan a popular version mixes soy sauce, rice vinegar, and wasabi.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Lemon juice provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Tomato ketchup and horseradish supply lycopene and glucosinolates with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Horseradish can stimulate bile production, potentially improving digestion.

items.title: High sugar and salt content
items.content: Ketchup and ready-made sauces often contain significant amounts of sugar and sodium, which may be problematic for hypertension or diabetes.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: While the sauce itself does not contain shellfish, it is usually served with them, posing a risk for allergic individuals.

items.title: Spicy horseradish
items.content: Horseradish can irritate the stomach lining in people with sensitivity.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the sauce with cold seafood (shrimp cocktail, crab sticks), use as a dip for fried fish, chicken nuggets, or vegetable sticks. It can also be added to marinades, salad dressings, or used as a base for more complex sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep opened cocktail sauce refrigerated in a sealed container. It stays fresh for 1–2 weeks. Discard if you notice off‑smell, color changes, or mold.
